pure-announcement.rationale: It is a first-person experiment memo about running local models for agentic coding, with no product launch, release, or funding content.

duplicate.rationale: None of the nearest concepts (Agent Skills format, acceptability-envelope evals, Code Mode, W2S sandbox, retrieval evals) cover local-model coding viability or its evaluation.

unfalsifiable.rationale: The author documents machines, models, settings, and links the open eval harness (birgitta410/local-coding-evals), so the results are reproducible in principle.

durability.rationale: The load-bearing findings are pass rates and rankings for specific model versions (Qwen3.6 35B MoE 2/2 vs Gemma 4 26B 0/3, 5/7 failures on 48GB vs 1/7 on 64GB) that the next model generation will invalidate, even though the seven-step viability funnel itself would age well.

actionability.rationale: It hands a reader a reusable seven-step viability funnel plus concrete task-fit heuristics — minimise discovery, point at files, keep instructions specific, pre-plan with a big model — that directly change how someone would trial a local coding setup.

atomicity.rationale: It interleaves at least two separable ideas — the viability funnel as an evaluation method and the task-characteristics that determine local-model fit — inside a narrative of experiment results, so no single paragraph states the core.
